dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study utilized four public datasets (Cam-CAN, OASIS-3, OpenBHB, HCP-YA) and one cohort from Newcastle University (NCL, categorized as SINGLE-SITE) to build the normative model. The BLISS dataset provided the clinical patient group and matched controls.

We also used a cohort of healthy adult participants scanned at Newcastle University as part of another study (site=NCL). ... Data were collected as part of the Bipolar Lithium Imaging and Spectroscopy Study (BLISS).

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The normative model of cortical thickness was developed using 6344 healthy individuals from five cohorts (Cam-CAN, OASIS-3, OpenBHB, HCP-YA, and NCL). BLISS BD patients (n=56) were the primary clinical target, and BLISS HCs (n=26) were used to adjust for site effects and were included in the normative reference.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: We utilised public datasets to develop normative models of cortical thickness (n = 5977) to generate robust estimations of cortical abnormalities in patients. ... Data were collected as part of the Bipolar Lithium Imaging and Spectroscopy Study (BLISS). ... We harmonised the normative-HC data, including the 26 HCs recruited to BLISS, for each ROI by regressing age, sex and scanning protocol (i.e., site; as a random effect) on cortical thickness
